newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares hold gains but eyes on Wall St.
newsitem.headline: German shares hold gains but eyes on Wall St.

text.p: German shares remained strongly ahead in post-bourse IBIS electronic dealings but were keeping a cautious eye on Wall Street before risking a further push upward.

The IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic dealings, edged up to 2,865.07 at 1400 GMT. The DAX had closed the floor session up 65.28 points, or 2.34 percent, at 2,857.24 points, eliminating more than half of its losses from Friday.
The gains came amid relief that last week's warnings against excessive market exuberance by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan did not have a disastrous impact on Wall Street.
Dealers said the mood in Frankfurt was mostly calm but some residual jitters from Friday were limiting the market's upside.
"We want to take another look at Wall Street," said one dealer. "Some people are still feeling a bit nervous looking forward."
Strong Bunds and the dollar's stability above 1.55 marks were boosting sentiment, however.
The main winners of the day were export-sensitive auto and chemical stocks, which had taken the worst beating along with the dollar in Friday's rout.
BASF was up 3.4 percent at 60.64 marks in afternoon trade.

Shares in Volkswagen AG, always volatile as the company's legal battle continues with GM over alleged industrial espionage, jumped briefly after VW said its chairman was poised to express his regrets to GM over the issue.
GM had made a public apology one of its conditions for any settlement of the court case. VW shares hit a high of 608.75, but then settled up 6.35 at 602.50, in line with the trend.

Dealers were divided on the market's next move. Some were confident that the traditional end-of-year rally will proceed after a short pause, while others believed the market would consolidate to reflect last week's dizzying highs and lows.
